title: The WLM galaxy on the edge of the Local Group
caption: The Wolf-Lundmark-Melotte galaxy, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: ESO's OmegaCAM camera on the VLT Survey Telescope captured this image of a solitary galaxy called Wolf-Lundmark-Melotte, or WLM for short. It lies in the direction of the constellation Cetus.
WLM belongs to our Local Group, the family of dozens of galaxies that includes the Milky Way. But it keeps its distance, sitting alone on the group's fringe as one of its farthest-flung members.

It is also small, and so isolated that it may never have interacted with another galaxy in the Local Group, and perhaps not with any other galaxy in the whole history of the Universe. Encounters between galaxies can stir up their gas and reshape them, so a galaxy that may have spent its whole history undisturbed is a notable case.

understand.summary: This image was made with OmegaCAM on the VLT Survey Telescope, using ultraviolet, green and red filters plus H-alpha. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is ultraviolet light, which the eye cannot see, and the galaxy is too faint to view this way without long exposures.

explore: The image was made as part of the VST/OmegaCAM Local Group Survey, using filters from the ultraviolet through visible light, including one that isolates glowing hydrogen.
